Content:
Ima be honest having worked retail in the past it's still possible the manager doesn't actually know him. Like I agree that it's better for customer relations to not allow such bulk purchases for a product you know will sell out regardless, but the reality is corporate likely doesn't have a rule about bulk purchases and in the end the manager is rewarded by the company just for overall sales for the location. So the quicker he can sell stuff the better his numbers look and that's really all it takes to allow the first guy that comes in whose willing to buy it all. Similarly I do understand not allowing others to take it once he's bringing it up it's really not much different than why you wouldn't be allowed to pull a product out of someone else's cart even though they haven't rung it up first.
Don't get me wrong, the dude buying is still shitty, and the manager knowing it was going to ultimately sell regardless probably shouldn't have allowed him to wheel up the shelves but in the end the likely hood that he doesn't know him and is just selling because all corporate cares about is numbers is very high.

Content: Yo @penguinz0 if you want to hear how bad it can be, just listen to this. I work as a department lead for a Fred Meyer store and I'm in charge of the pokemon (along well all other cards). Author: @AfterBucket6491
Content:
I’ve always been a Pokémon fan. From cards, games, shows, ect. My sister love her older brothers (me and my older brother) who both love Pokémon. I turned 18 and got a good job and had a lot of spending cash and my sister has been wanting Pokémon cards. Every time i go to the store the shelves are EMPTY except for the toys. 
One morning, I went to my neighborhood Walmart to print some photos I had took. This was at like 11am and photos were done at 11:30. As I was walking away from the Photo Booth, I see a worker stocking the pokemon shelves, and I lit up like a firework! I was so happy to see a full shelf of cards to choose from and look at to get card for my sister and me! As I was waiting for the worker to finish, three guys come up and push past me and start grabbing everything they can! The worker told them to stop or he’ll call security and got on his radio and called anyhow. The three guys then put everything back and wait with me. When security comes and waits for the worker to Finnish, they leave and they said we were good to grab what we wanted. I walked up to look at what packs they had. And before I was able to grab one of the new trainer packs they grabbed it out of my hand and 80% of the shelves. 
There were only those already open packs of cards that are in that hot wheels looking box. 

I wanted to cry, but the worker came from the other aisle and put up too big boxes, opened them, and said “here, you can grab what you want from these if you want!” I hugged him outta emotion and apologized and said thank you over and over. I got to get that purple box trainer box for my sister with some of those three pack cards with the coin and one of those big card packs with gangar as a huge mega ex card! I got a lot from those boxes and was happy I was able too. 
My sister now is able to have 3 full decks, one she likes using is that  bolt hound ex. 

Anyhow I just wanted to share and say that we need limits on how many pokemon card items per person. I’m 20 now and I know I might be “too old” to collect and or even play. But I like to get cards sometimes and have the thrill of getting cool cards or building better decks! 

The best feeling and moment I had was discovering those pokemon vending machines and it actually being filled. I bought a single booster pack and got a gold pokeball card! I was super stoked. But again, people buy all the cards and I haven’t found another one with cards since. 
Bring back good pokemon community so me and my little sister can play!

The issue is, people will always pay the scalper price; someone out there, even collectors, will eventually hit at whatever price for things as mainstream as pokemon. There’s so many fans and so much potential for fomo that its the perfect supply demand situation for scalping- there will always be people that even applaud it for raising the “bid” and value of the items. Its horrible but its greed from both the top end consumer’s (as in not all consumers, we understand we do what we do for the little ones or really bottle necked items like consoles but there will always be some sweaty value collector out there wanting to gouge things or happily buy something for the sake of it being pricey) as well as the scalpers themselves. 

Its something thats played out quite a lot in many nerd hobbies before as well and still does today, especially competitive collection card games.

Former Walmart associate for context, I worked front end, Cap-2 (unload trucks/stock/backroom), OPD, kinda everything but especially to do with the backroom.

Author: @adreiiaii510
Content:
I found out a friend of mine got into this back during the pandemic after she lost her job. She had thousands in gambling debt, along with rising credit card debt and back rent. Somehow, she was able to get a $10,000 loan and went nuts cleaning out a Target. She was being "coached" by an "expert" she met on Reddit, who told her how to get the money to start, where to go and what to buy (i.e. what stores sold it the cheapest at the time), how to sell it, etc. The "expert" claimed they were making six figures flipping product. (sound familiar? lol)

She flipped it on eBay and made ... *drumroll* ... -$1,800 in losses (basically stuck eating costs of shipping, back-charges, etc.). Her "expert" offered to "hire" her to go mass buy product the expert would then flip and pay her 20% of the profit. She did that for a bit but wasn't making anywhere near what she needed to in order to pay off debts, rent or even buy food.

She got out when she started feeling desperate enough to get into fights at stores to horde product. Believe her and her boyfriend filed for bankruptcy as well (don't talk to them anymore).

These people are lunatics with no business sense, or in some other cases, victims of pyramid scams.

Author: @byrdfinger
Content:
I'm not defending the guy, but I don't know what world y'all live in that other customers are allowed to take items out of other customer's carts or off of the belt as they're ringing it up...? Y'all are nuts for acting like the workers should support the act of helping one customer take items from another customers cart/purchase. 
I'm from New Orleans where we have hurricanes and mandatory evacuations, and when that happens the stores and gas stations get mauled by shoppers who buy all the water, food, and gas. It's first come first serve. And guess what, the majority is bought by small amounts of people and the majority of us get there 30 min to late and the shelves are empty and you have to walk by the insanely long lines of people with mountains of food and water in their baskets as they wait to get rung up. And no worker is gonna help you take a pack of water out of someone's cart for yourself. And if you try, you'll either get shot, knocked out, and/or kicked out of the store. And if the workers support anyone it will be the person who had the items first. -->SOME<-- stores set limits for how many packs of water you can buy, but that is the small exception of stores. More often than not, it's first come first serve because that's how stores work.
I've never seen an entire group of people like y'all who are backing the idea of forcefully taking items from somebody who's in the process of purchasing them. And the fact that y'all are dumbfounded as to why the store would not help another customer take the items for himself is fkn wild!
Now, it'd be one thing if the store hadset maximum purchase limits to the items beforehand, and I think the stores should, in fact, do that in circumstances such as these, but they did NOT do that. 
So, it's wild that y'all are in such bewilderment about thats simply not how commerce works in this country. 
Y'all are fkn wiiiiiild.

Author: @torq3266
Content:
When I worked at Walmart, I was early morning shift, before the store opened. Sometimes the cards were stocked when I clocked in so I would take a box and hide it somewhere else in the store. I love collecting these cards, it's a small hobby of mine. I had to start doing that because of these people trying to hog all of them to themselves.

If you work at Walmart, here's my advice if you want to hide one for yourself to still be able to enjoy the hobby.

Hide the cards behind the mattresses. The only people who buy mattresses are usually just moving in. It's one of those one-time purchases that lasts at least a decade, so not many people are coming in to buy them. So nobody's going to see a box of pokemon cards behind the mattresses. Another place I hid them was in trash cans, only the cans that are broken, and if I can move them behind all the other trash cans. That one is way more iffy though since people buy more trash cans than they do mattresses.

Content: I'm not a lawyer, but I was always lead to believe, as a child, that ticket scalping wasn't just something to shame people for, my understanding was that it was ILLEGAL. It sounds like the only real way to fix this fucking problem is to get legislation to extend scalping laws to trading cards. If its illegal to flip tickets, then we can make it fucking illegal to flip trading cards. It's up to the communities built around trading cards to decide what they want that to look like, whether all retail locations selling cards are required to put a hard cap on packs sold to individuals, or if making the act of reselling card packs (obv not single cards) a form of illegal scalping. I understand that how the community goes about it could have an impact on small card shops, so its not my place to suggest an exact methodology, but long story short, the trading card community needs to rally together on how to exactly change the law to make this specific act of cruelty illegal, and you guys need to get with the lawmakers to make these changes. Author: @Blargleflakes
Content:
Story time! I recently got into the hobby, as an attempt to sell the cards me and my brother acquired when we were children. We have a lot of cards so many are worth less than a dollar. In an attempt to avoid the effort of selling a bunch of these cheaper ones on eBay, I took it to my local trading shop for appraisal.

They had a ton of positive reviews, and even my buddy endorsed them, so I thought I could trust them. They claim they pay between 50 and 85% of market value on their website but in classic bait and switch style on their terms and conditions it’s 40 and 85%. 

I shrug this off, because many businesses use bait and switch tactics. They even said that my cards looked good and that vintage cards typically air on the higher side of that range, so I said sure let’s get them appraised.

350 vintage common/uncommon cards lightly to moderately played, so I expected the appraisal, according to their terms of conditions, to be anywhere from 32 to like 90 or so dollars. 

They come back to me with an appraisal of 28$, less than 40% of mkt value and violating the terms and conditions that they had already changed once before. 

Oh, and they lost the Tupperware I brought it in, and gave me 35$ store credit….for a Tupperware….a Tupperware 

Yea I think Charlie might be on to something. Needless to say I took my cards back 😂

Author: @NemesisMKIII
Content:
My best friend was a manager at EB Games (Gamestop) up here in Canada, at the busiest location. When it came to Pokemon Cards, they had a strict purchase limit policy and you had to be put on a list with your ID to purchase them. This wasn't her policy, it was corporate. Now, she also is a wizard at tracking things online, so when she'd sell packs, after every shift she would go online and search all the local sites to see who was just scalping and add them to the list of no-sales. MANY times people came into buy more packs and they were flat-out denied service and corporate had her back every time. It was glorious. I am not a conspiracy man by any means, but I believe that manager is 100% colluding with that shopper and this should be brought to corporates' attention, because it's a bad look when you sell all your stock to one customer and potentially drives off other sales in the future. 
I know TCG people are passionate about their hobby, but people they are piece of cardboard, and designed for kids and to be played with. People who turn hobbies into speculation markets are trash. I collect comic books, and I've seen what it did to our second-hand market and the crash it can create in it. I understand everyone wants to have a hustle and make money on the side, but when your pursuit of profits destroys the very hobby itself, you're trash. Eventually this pokemon bubble WILL burst as much as people think it won't, it will and then all you'll have is your pieces of cardboard and a lifetime of bas investments. 
I am trying to be polite here, but honestly these people are gross and I feel bad for all the kids these days trying to get into the hobby and enjoy it when it's a bunch of grown ass adults who are just trying to milk their hobby for some extra cash because they don't want to get an actual job.

Author: @gingerbread3686
Content:
I see a lot of people commenting and asking why buying the whole inventory of cards is bad for the Walmart or why they wouldnt allow it. They want to sell their product so whats the issue?
The issue is that any retail store purchases inventory based on very good estimates on what is going to be bought. Especially with items that have no expiry date this means their stock is likely to be bought out sooner rather than later. 
This is to say: there is no real risk of them not selling these items. However what can be damaging to a store is lacking product availability and customer satisfaction. A retail store like walmart lives off the fact that they have the exact product a customer is looking for. If less products become available because of one huge purchase that is much more damaging long term and the reason why stores dont like these unannounced huge purchases. If youre looking to buy large amounts of one product you can always call your local retail store to ask them to make a large purchase when restocking, allowing you to essentially order more stock for you to buy. This is an actual thing stores do. (Doesnt work with inherently limited items like these cards but most other items work)

Author: @plague696
Content: As someone who used to work at Wal-Mart it's tough to say if the dude in the video is in on it or not. He very well could be. That is possibe but, I have seen many situations similar to this just with smaller PDQs ( the displays the cards were on are called that and there ones that are small enough to fit on a shelf) like we had 3 PDQs of Chromecast that had gone on sale and this scalper and demanded all of them. Worst part, there was another customer waiting at the same lock case they were displayed in waiting for help getting just one of those Chromecast. We were really busy so unfortunately it took a bit to get over there. My coworker at the time got there since I was stuck helping someone else. The scalper asked for all of them anyway. We called a manager as the other customer plead his case for one. Unfortunately, the policy is first come first serve so the manager told us to sell all of them to the scalper. After the scalper left my coworker pulled a Chromecast from behind our counter and sold it to the customer that had been pleading. Turns out while the scalper was dealing with the manager trying to stop the other customer from getting anything my coworker took one out of the PDQ and hid it behind the counter so the other guy could get one. Management only cares if a sale is made. That was the only way we could help customers that were getting screwed. So it is also possible that the manager isn't in on it and is just making a sale. I have seen done with PS5s and Xboxes, phones, tablets, laptops, etc. We use to have scalpers empty our entire lock up of laptops. It gets bad without the need of manager being in on it. It's really sad. I hated it then and I hate it now.

"I dont think they would let me buy the entire F___ shelf".

Only to hear ( i work evenings) that a scalper came in ( they usually use their tax exempt card) that morning and brought carts full. Author: @XArc7AngelX
Content:
How to stop guys like this:

1. Brick stores (Walmart, Target, etc.) need to put purchase limits on product.
2. DON'T BUY ON FACEBOOK MARKET PLACE.
3. If you buy on Amazon, buy directly from the card manufacturer, and make sure it's the verified Amazon shop.
4. Shop at local card shops you trust - check market values for the product you're purchasing. Good card shops won't typically charge more than 10%-15% over the market value (or at least this is what I've seen in my area and experience). It also helps to shop at card shops that host game tournaments for the cards you're interested in. 

And finally

5. STOP BELIEVING THE LIE THAT CARDS ARE A GOOD FINANCIAL INVESTMENT! They are not! If you're getting into the hobby for financial gain, YOU WILL GO BROKE. It's incredibly addictive and dangerous if you get into collecting with the wrong intentions.

Author: @ItzInsaneZzz
Content:
If he stopped someone else who was "waiting" to get the cards, then maybe you could say something about him buying all the cards. Scalping or not, you should be able to buy as much stock as you can afford. This wasn't a "prank-buy" making the employees bring all the goods to the counter to not buy any cards at all, he is "buying" the cards fair and square. If he told someone else they can't buy any while they are in the pokemon card aisle waiting to be stocked, then you could complain about the guy buying all those cards. This would be like me buying all the carrots in stock on the shelves and in the back, then bringing it to the counter to scan and pay; then someone else (another customer, doesn't matter who they are.) tries to come and grab a bag of carrots from the pile I'm trying to buy and take a bunch to try and purchase for whatever they may need it for. If I want to not share a single bag of carrots and eat all or sell all of the carrots after doesn't matter as long as I have enough money to buy every bag of carrots that are at the register. If I can't afford to buy a certain amount of bags of carrots after they are scanned, then anyone else can feel free to buy them. Kindergarten example right here. 💯 

The manager isn't in on no Scalp Scheme, he is doing his job. 💯

Also, he could just be a hard-core pokemon card collector who wants to have as many chances as possible to get a rare card, buying that many cards doesn't mean you are a scalper. The only thing that matters is whether he can afford to buy all the cards, even if he can't afford them, other people need to wait until they scan as much as he can buy and he leaves.
